albums.blurb: Recorded at Columbia's 30th Street Studio in New York over three sessions in the summer of 1959, Time Out was the Brubeck quartet's experiment in time signatures from outside the jazz mainstream: “Blue Rondo à la Turk” adapts a 9/8 Turkish aksak rhythm the band encountered on a State Department tour, and Paul Desmond's “Take Five” swings entirely in 5/4. It is the defining statement of the classic lineup — Brubeck on piano, Desmond on alto saxophone, Eugene Wright on bass and Joe Morello on drums — and the whole record is instrumental quartet jazz.
albums.reception: The album reached No. 2 on the Billboard albums chart and became the first jazz album to sell a million copies, while “Take Five” reached No. 25 on the pop singles chart in 1961 on its way to becoming the first million-selling jazz single.

albums.blurb: Cibo Matto were Yuka Honda and Miho Hatori, two Japanese-born musicians working in New York's downtown scene: Hatori sang while Honda built the tracks from keyboards, samples and sound collages. Viva! La Woman, their 1996 debut for Warner Bros., was produced with Mitchell Froom and Tchad Blake and recorded partly at Electric Lady Studios, and nearly every song is named for food — “Apple,” “Beef Jerky,” “Birthday Cake,” “Artichoke” — delivered over loops that swerve between hip-hop, bossa nova and lounge pop.
albums.reception: Spin ranked it the 10th-best album of 1996 and it placed 27th in that year's Village Voice Pazz & Jop critics' poll, while spending six weeks at No. 1 on CMJ's college radio chart.

albums.blurb: Gillian Welch records as a duo with guitarist David Rawlings, singing spare, close-harmony Americana rooted in Appalachian balladry, old-time and bluegrass. Time (The Revelator), her third album and the first released on the pair's own Acony label, was produced by Rawlings and cut largely live at Nashville's historic RCA Studio B; its songs turn the old-time palette toward slow meditations on American myth — Lincoln, the Titanic, John Henry, Elvis — and close with the fourteen-minute “I Dream a Highway.”
albums.reception: The album was nominated for Best Contemporary Folk Album at the 2002 Grammy Awards, and Paste later ranked it No. 7 on its list of the 50 best albums of the 2000s.
